q6.answer: The server looks up (device id, change id) in applied_changes first, in each change's own transaction, before it reads the version or locks the note. If the pair is found, it returns the stored result and writes nothing, so a retry never applies the same change twice.

q7.answer: The phone records it in sync_cursor, the last change log seq it has applied. The cursor moves only in the same local transaction that applies a download page, so a partly applied page never moves it.

q8.answer: The run ends and the cursor stays where it was. The whole page is fetched again at the next run (60 s timer, reconnect or foreground), starting with the upload step. Because each page is applied in one transaction, a partial page is never recorded as done.

q9.answer: The conflict result tells the phone its change was saved as a conflict, and the phone deletes that outbox row. The phone does not store the N2 id from the result. N2 and the server's copy of N arrive on the next download, which creates N2 and replaces local N when the entry's version is higher.

q10.answer: A queued change leaves the outbox when its result arrives: accepted, conflict, or the stored result for a retry. A row that gets a server error, or has no result after a dropped or lost response, stays in the outbox and is sent again at the next run.

q11.answer: The download replaces the local body and version of the note when the entry's version is higher, even if a row for it is pending. The pending row keeps its own body and base, so its later upload conflicts and is saved as a conflict note. Whether the UI should keep showing the pending edit is an open point and is not decided.

q12.answer: The sent or sending row is never changed. The new edit goes into a new queued row with base set to the last applied version, and that row shows in the UI. The sent row uploads first with its stored result, and the new row then conflicts once the server has moved past its base.
